claims.text: Modeling atomic-level disorder and anharmonic lattice interactions will predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional averaging methods.
The relevant as-synthesized high-entropy alloys possess complex atomic arrangements and chemical disorder.
Chemical disorder produces atomic-level bonding variations and local vibrational modes.
Anharmonic interactions influence local vibrational modes in high-entropy alloys.
Explicitly capturing local structural heterogeneity reduces the averaging errors of conventional thermal-conductivity methods.
Explicitly capturing anharmonic lattice dynamics reduces the averaging errors of conventional thermal-conductivity methods.
Modeling local structural heterogeneity and anharmonic dynamics yields more precise predictions of phonon scattering.
More precise modeling of phonon scattering will produce a lower predicted thermal conductivity.
The advanced approach will reduce prediction error margins by approximately 10–30% relative to conventional methods.
Conventional predictive methods use averaged phonon dispersion relations.
Conventional predictive methods do not explicitly account for atomic-scale disorder or anharmonic effects.
The approach is primarily applicable to high-entropy alloys with substantial chemical disorder.
The approach may not extend to alloys with strong phase separation or chemical ordering.
Prediction improvement depends on the details of the computational model.
Prediction improvement depends on the degree of chemical disorder in the alloy.
